messages:
olivia.tran: FYI customer reporting onboarding/SCIM sync weirdness — users created but missing roles and ~5 service accounts marked as 'orphaned'. They hit errors when we try to re-run provisioning. escalation to security/compliance.
raj.patel: Can you paste the error they see or a correlation id? Also which KMS (aws/gcp/hsm) is configured for that tenant?
olivia.tran: Correlation ID: c-0a9f3b2. They are on our default managed KMS (AWS KMS) with a customer-provided key alias. When we repro locally we see decrypt failures.
maria.gonzalez: Logged into infra and pulled the recent provisioning job logs for tenant t-acme-01. Snippet:
```
ERROR provisioning: decrypt failed: kms.Decrypt failed: HSM_KEY_NOT_FOUND (key id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/7f4a1c)
cause: key metadata not found in keyring
stack: runtime/provision.go:241
```
sec-oncall: That's consistent with an edge case where a key alias was deleted/rotated outside our flow. Two immediate questions: 1) did SCIM create any plain-text artifacts (should be no), 2) do we have audit log entries for the KMS Decrypt calls around the timestamp?
olivia.tran: Customer insists they didn't touch keys. They also say their SSO assertions intermittently failed in the same time window (SAML 500 on auth callback). They provided the SAML request id: SAML-req-821. I'll attach their export in the support ticket.
raj.patel: For repro in staging I need the tenant config (scim enabled, scim_version, sso_provider, kms_alias). Also please include the exact request payload used to provision the service accounts.
olivia.tran: Sending payload in a sec. Sample repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/t-acme-01/provision \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"scim_sync":true,"create_service_accounts":true,"sso_idp":"okta","kms_alias":"alias/customer/t-acme-01"}'
```
maria.gonzalez: Quick check: our audit retention policy for the hosted tier is 30d by default. The customer has a compliance requirement for 90d. Their events from ~45d ago may have been purged. We do have an export job we can run if leadership approves elevated retention for a window.
sec-oncall: Approval path: need a written request from customer + SOC approval. I can fast-track the audit export for the correlation id if legal approves. Meanwhile mitigation: rotate to a new KMS key and re-encrypt the provisioning secrets (we can do a manual key import flow). That will unblock new provisioning but won't recover already-orphaned service accounts.
raj.patel: For investigating the orphaned accounts we should capture a full repro in a sandbox that mirrors their KMS alias deletion scenario. Steps:
1) create tenant with same config
2) provision normally
3) simulate key alias removal (delete alias or change key policy)
4) attempt repro provisioning -> capture logs/traces
I can spin that up if someone drops me the exact alias and timestamps.
olivia.tran: Dropping alias and timestamps to the ticket now. Customer offered to let us run non-prod repro against a staging replica of their config — they gave consent for debugging.
sec-oncall: Also recommend exporting audit logs for all KMS-related API calls for that tenant for the 14-day window around the incident (if available). If retention purged them we can pull CloudTrail S3 archives (if configured). Please open an internal ticket to request infra access to the CloudTrail bucket: infra-ticket-5421.
maria.gonzalez: Noted. I'll queue the export and add retention change request. ETA: 6 hours for initial export, 24-48h for wider retrieval if archived.
deploy-bot: auto:deploy-notice - provisioning-service v2.14 deployed to staging at 1765432200
raj.patel: Small patch we should check: ensure our graceful failure returns a retryable error and includes the original KMS key id in the response so ops can escalate to the customer's cloud admin. Right now response is generic 500.
olivia.tran: Agreed. For customer-facing immediate workaround I suggested: 1) rotate to a new KMS alias we control, 2) re-run provisioning flow to recreate service accounts (with explicit role mapping), 3) once audit export is available we can map which users were missed and reconcile. Customer asked for written runbook — I'll draft steps and share.
sec-oncall: I'll take ownership of the audit export and coordinate with legal. Raj and Maria, tag me if you need IAM perms to access the CloudTrail bucket.
olivia.tran: Thanks everyone. Next: I will post the runbook + ticket links and update the customer within 2 hours. :thumbsup:
